title: Maevarano Formation, Madagascar: Majungasaurus
summary: In the Maastrichtian, about 70–66 million years ago, northwestern Madagascar was home to Majungasaurus, an abelisaurid theropod that was the apex predator and preyed on sauropods such as Rapetosaurus. Its fossils come from the Maevarano Formation of the Mahajanga Basin, whose bone beds near Berivotra record mass deaths in a semiarid landscape a few tens of metres below the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary.

uncertainty.note: Range is the temporal range given for Majungasaurus; the sources date the formation only to the Maastrichtian.
